artworks.title: Narcissus
artworks.description: Caravaggio isolates Ovid's hunter at the pool: a single figure bent over his own reflection, knee and sleeve catching the only light in an otherwise black void. Desire and doom collapse into one circular composition — the youth already trapped by the image that will waste him into a flower. Oil on canvas, Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica (Palazzo Barberini), Rome.

artworks.title: Echo and Narcissus
artworks.description: Waterhouse stages the double tragedy of Metamorphoses Book III: Narcissus stretched beside a forest pool, lost in his reflection, while the nymph Echo watches helplessly from the rocks. The Pre-Raphaelite landscape makes the Thespian spring both beautiful and fatal. Oil on canvas, Walker Art Gallery, Liverpool.

artworks.title: Echo and Narcissus
artworks.description: Poussin's classical pastoral shows Narcissus already fading by the water while Echo collapses in grief and a putto mourns nearby — Ovid's metamorphosis rendered as ordered landscape tragedy. The youth who loved only himself becomes part of the still pool that destroyed him. Oil on canvas, Musée du Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Narcissus
artworks.description: This Milanese Renaissance panel presents Narcissus as a half-length youth leaning over a stone basin, his face mirrored in the water — the myth reduced to its essential trap of sight and self. Long associated with Leonardo's circle through Boltraffio, the painting holds the National Gallery, London.

films.title: Narcissus
films.description: McLaren's National Film Board ballet short dances the hunter into his own reflection — experimental cinema restaging Ovid's pool without a spoken word.

popCulture.title: Narcissism
popCulture.description: Psychology took the hunter's name for self-absorption — from clinical narcissistic personality to everyday 'narcissist' — so the pool at Thespiae still names a modern diagnosis.

popCulture.title: Narcissus (plant)
popCulture.description: The daffodil genus keeps the myth in every spring garden: Ovid's youth who wasted into a flower still blooms as narcissus along roadsides and in florist shops.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's sequel brings Narcissus back as a vain, pool-bound shade — the hunter still admiring himself while the underworld war rages past.
